note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/axis/math500-01/vectors.json + manifest.json, studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. The manifest has no 'model' field; the model is identified from each arm's 'what' text: M30 = math30_cue ('Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0), cue', prompt cue), M31 = rl_cue (present, 'RL-Zero-Math 3.1, cue'). Vectors are v3 0/1 aligned through problem_indices; missing counts 0 (none expected, all 500 present). Q4 = ranks 376-500 after sorting by (t2_generated_tokens, problem_index); T2 cap hits sit at their stored count (16,384), so they all fall in Q4. Statistic = sum M31 - sum M30 over Q4; bootstrap over the 125 Q4 problems (pairs). Not a group contrast (same problems, two arms), so no groups line; n = 125. Alt reading: Q4 by value threshold, including every problem tied with the rank-376 length (equals the main number if no tie crosses the boundary). Caveat: T2 is the rl plain sample, a different sampling of 3.1 than the rl_cue arm scored here, as the recipe intends.

Same files and arm choice as k 1 (math30_cue vs rl_cue, identified via the manifest 'what' text since there is no model field). Short half = ranks 1-250 by (t2_generated_tokens, problem_index). Statistic = sum M31 - sum M30 over those 250; bootstrap over the 250 problems; n = 250. Refuted if measured > 5. Alt reading: short half by value threshold, including every problem tied with the rank-250 length.

Files: s3 r3/fr-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (A, 3.0) and r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B, 3.1 step 2,800), fetched to runs/theory-tests/r3/<run>/out/, plus per_problem.json. Keep sample == 0, first row per problem_index; S = problems kept in both with cap_hit false in both; r = ln(max(n_new_A,1)/max(n_new_B,1)). Q4 = T2 ranks 376-500, short half = ranks 1-250 over all 500 per_problem rows (ranks not recomputed within S). statistics.median gives mean of the two middle values for even counts. Groups line gives the S sizes in Q4 and short half; n = smaller one; fewer than 20 in either -> refuted_without_number. Bootstrap resamples the S problems that lie in Q4 or short half (Q3 problems do not enter the statistic); a resample with an empty group would return 0.0 (practically impossible at these sizes). Alt reading (unpaired): per group ln(median finished n_new of 3.0 / median finished n_new of 3.1), each model's finished rows taken on its own without requiring the other model to finish. Caveat: excluding problems where either model hit the cap removes the longest problems mostly from Q4, which can bias the Q4 median toward problems both finished; the fr-01 run used the 3.1 tokenizer and prompt (known confound).

Files: s3 r3/fr-01/out/{P,F}_math500.jsonl (3.0) and r3/s2800-01/out/{P,F}_math500.jsonl (3.1), in runs/theory-tests/r3/. Each file: sample == 0, first row per problem_index, then cap_hit false only; P and F pooled per model. A_m = count 8000 <= n_new < 12000, B_m = count n_new >= 12000; statistic (B30/A30)/(B31/A31). If A30, A31 or B31 is 0 -> refuted_without_number. B30 = 0 gives measured 0 (defined, not refuted). Groups line gives the four counts; n = the smallest of the four counts (the tail counts are what the ratio depends on; it can be small). Bootstrap: one entry per problem_index holding that problem's kept finished rows across the four files; a resample where the ratio is undefined returns +inf, so the upper interval end may print as Infinity. Alt reading: the same with n_generated (= n_new + 1 in the rows seen) instead of n_new, which only moves rows sitting exactly at the 8,000 / 12,000 boundaries. example_row has the text and prefill_ids fields removed for size.
